ClaimHistoryEntry.description: One claim in a session's history.

release_reason.description: Why it ended. Absent if it had not ended when the record was assembled.

released_at.description: When it ended (UTC). Absent if it had not ended when the record was assembled.

ClaimId.description:
Identifier of a claim.

Starts with `clm_`.

anyOf.description: One symbol (function, class, method, ...) within a file.

symbol.description: Repository-relative path of the file that contains the symbol.

symbol_path.description: The symbol's path inside the file, segments joined by `.`.

ClaimScope.description:
What a claim covers: a whole file, or one symbol inside a file.

On the wire this is `{"file": "<path>"}` or `{"symbol": "<path>", "symbol_path": "<a.b.c>"}`.

ContentHash.description: A content hash: the lowercase hex SHA-256 digest (64 characters) of a file's bytes.

EndedReason.description: Why a session record was finalized.

oneOf.description: The harness reported the end of the session.

No end event arrived; the record was assembled later and `ended_at` is the last time the
seat was seen.

FileChange.description: A file a session changed, with content hashes before and after.

post_hash.description: Hash of the content after the session's last change. `null` if the file was deleted.

pre_hash.description: Hash of the content before the session's first change. `null` if the file did not exist.

GuardDecisions.description: Summary of the gate's decisions during a session.

counts.description: How many times each reason code was returned. Codes never returned are omitted.

notable.description: The denials and prompts worth reading individually, oldest first.

LoreId.description:
Identifier of a lore entry, chosen when the entry is created and stable afterwards.

Starts with `lore_`.

NotableDecision.description: A guard decision worth listing individually in the record.

path_or_command.description:
The repository-relative path or, for shell commands, the command text that triggered the
decision. Recorders MUST NOT store secrets here (records sync to the git remote) and
SHOULD truncate long commands.

reason_code.description: Why the engine decided as it did.

Outcome.description: What the harness should do with the tool call.

oneOf.description: Let the tool call proceed.
Block the tool call. `message` tells the agent why and what to do instead.
Ask the human to approve in the harness's own prompt.

Reserved for deferred edits, which a later revision of the spec will define.
Implementations MUST NOT emit it before then; consumers that do not support it MUST treat
it as `deny`.

OverrideId.description:
Identifier of a human override, which lets agents change files in `owned` zones they do
not own.

Starts with `ovr_`.

OverrideMode.description: How long a human override lasts.

oneOf.description: One tool call: the first call that needs the override uses it up.
The rest of the session of the first seat that uses it.

OverrideUse.description:
A human override a session used: the pilot let the session's agent change files in `owned`
zones it does not own.

granted_by.description: The human who granted it, identified by git email address.

paths.description: The files the session changed or claimed under it, each once, in order of first use.

pattern.description: The glob the override covers, repository-relative.

ReasonCode.description:
A stable machine-readable code saying why the engine decided as it did.

The set is closed: a new code is a spec change. The typical outcome of each code is listed in
the spec's reason-code table and by [`ReasonCode::typical_outcomes`].

oneOf.description: Nothing is blocked. Outcome `allow`.

`acs off` is active for this repository; the gate is disabled except for sealed paths,
banned commands and self-protection. Outcome `allow`.

A target matches a sealed glob or zone, or reaches a protected location outside the
repository; or a command with unknown effects mentions one. Always denied for agents.
Outcome `deny`.

A shell command matches a `destructive.ban` pattern, or breaks a self-protection rule
(running state-changing `acs` commands, skipping git hooks, starting a harness with its
hooks off). Always denied. Outcome `deny`.
A history rewrite or force push targets a protected branch. Outcome `deny`.

A write, delete or move target cannot be resolved, or resolves outside the repository but
links back into it; with `protect_outside_repo`, any target outside the repository root.
Outcome `ask`.
Deletes exceed `destructive.max_files_deleted_outside_claims`. Outcome `deny`.
Deletes in one command exceed `destructive.max_files_deleted_per_command`. Outcome `ask`.
A destructive shell command whose targets cannot be determined. Outcome `ask`.

An overlapping live claim is held by another seat (claim rules, spec section 8).
Outcome `deny`.

An agent whose pilot is not an owner wrote or deleted a file in an `owned` zone, and no
human override covers it. Outcome `deny`.

The state database is locked, corrupt or missing. Outcome `deny` for destructive actions,
otherwise `allow` with a warning.
The adapter could not parse the harness payload. Outcome `allow`.

An edit was queued because of a claim conflict. Reserved together with the `queue`
outcome; implementations MUST NOT return it yet. Outcome `queue`.
The holder released it explicitly.
It ran past its TTL without a heartbeat.
It was released because the session ended.

RepoPath.description:
A repository-relative path in a stored record.

Uses forward slashes as separators, is relative to the repository root and is never empty.
A value is invalid if it is empty, starts with `/` or `\`, or starts with a Windows drive
letter (`C:`). Producers MUST also normalize paths (no `.` or `..` segments, symlinks
resolved, case folded where the filesystem is case-insensitive); validators cannot check that.

Seat.description:
One agent session (or human editing session) working in a repository.

There is exactly one seat per harness session. A seat is created on the first event of a
session.

branch.description: The checked-out branch. Absent when HEAD is detached.

harness.description: Name of the harness, for example `claude-code`.

last_seen_at.description: When the seat last produced an event (UTC).

pilot.description: The pilot (the human responsible for the seat), identified by git email address.

target_branch.description:
The branch this work will be integrated into. Claims only conflict within one target
branch.

worktree.description:
Absolute path of the worktree the seat works in. In a session record, only the name of
the worktree's folder: records are pushed, and absolute paths carry user names.

SeatId.description:
Identifier of a seat: one agent session (or human editing session) working in a repository.

Starts with `seat_`.

SessionId.description:
Identifier of a session record. This is the value carried by the `ACS-Session` commit trailer.

Starts with `ses_`.

SpecVersion.description:
The `spec` field of a document: the version of the ACS spec it was written against.

The only supported value is `"acs/0.1"`. Readers MUST reject any other value.

SymbolPath.description:
The path of a symbol within its file, as segments joined by `.`.

For example `Refunds.apply` names the method `apply` of the class `Refunds`. Every segment is
non-empty. One symbol path *contains* another when its segments are a prefix of the other's
(a symbol contains itself).

description:
The ledger entry for one session: who worked, what was claimed, what changed, what was denied.

Records are synced to the git remote, so they hold only structural data (paths, hashes,
counts), never prompts.

acs_version.description: Version of the `acs` binary that wrote the record.

claims.description: Every claim the seat held, in acquisition order.

commits.description: Full hashes of the commits that carry this session's `ACS-Session` trailer.

ended_at.description: When the session ended (UTC). For crashed sessions, the last time the seat was seen.

intent.description: What the agent said it was doing, from the `acs_intent` tool. Absent if never declared.

lore_loaded.description: Lore entries injected into the session.

overrides.description: Human overrides the session used. Omitted when there were none.

seat.description: The seat the session ran on.

session_id.description: Identifier of the record; the value of the `ACS-Session` commit trailer.

spec.description: The spec version this record conforms to. Always `acs/0.1`.

title: SessionRecord
